architecture_transcribed.consolidation_at_scale: replay through the same local rule that wrote the engrams (Hebbian co-activation with Oja-style normalization) at tiers 120 and 300, with interference measured against the MP-E8 curriculum
architecture_transcribed.seconds_working_memory: plasticize the central-complex loop into a decayed activation trace over the last k tokens; a fast-weight state computed by spread, replacing unigram context; parameterize k and register its sweep

selection_two_native_routing_variants_bo.variant_i: scores candidates by spread of the decayed state plus target-organ injection (the target organ already injects into speak_sentence and is hereby actually used for selection)
selection_two_native_routing_variants_bo.variant_ii: routes candidates through carve as an allowed_pools mask, the version closest to existing machinery
selection_two_native_routing_variants_bo.why_this_one_is_primary: the plan itself designates variant (ii) as 'the version closest to existing machinery', and 6.3 requires one variant registered primary and the other the ablation. The choice is made before any treatment and against a property of the code, not against a result. If the PI prefers (i) as primary, say so before the first run is scored -- swapping primary and ablation afterwards is an R2 event.

candidate_routing_step3.both_variants_built_neither_chosen: variant_i fills engine.decide's `extra_drive` with amplitude pairs from the spread of the decayed state (the target-organ injection route, engine.py's own words: 'how a scent, a body state or a voice enters alongside the words ... through the fly's own wiring rather than around it'). variant_ii fills `allowed_pools` with the pools the trace currently resonates with, floored at 3 of 12 so a near-empty state cannot leave the carve with a decision that has no alternatives. Both are existing parameters of an existing method -- neither variant invents a mechanism, which is what the registration means by 'native'.
candidate_routing_step3.checklist_step: B.4 step 3: 'Implement both candidate-routing variants behind flags: spread-scored selection, and carve allowed_pools masking; register the primary and the ablation.'
candidate_routing_step3.does_not_establish: No H1 or H2 verdict, no k-sweep extension, no tier, no scored run, no answer to D-MPE10-02, -03, -04 or -05. The gate's `go_if` is 'H1-H4 hold' and H2 still has no scalar.
candidate_routing_step3.flag: MP_E10_ROUTING = off | variant_i | variant_ii | both; default off. An unrecognised value raises rather than falling back silently, and `off` is the legacy unigram path kept runnable for comparison as ablations_required demands -- it is the ablation's third condition, not a neutral setting. The `off` arm scores against the unigram context OF THE SEQUENCE, not of the candidate list; scoring candidates against their own mean would be circular and would flatter the baseline.
candidate_routing_step3.named_missing_house_wiring: The two variants are implemented as selection rules over a labelled candidate geometry; they are NOT yet wired into the live organ. The wiring points are real and already exist -- `connectome/engine.py:110 decide(code, text, allowed_pools, extra_drive)` and the `scent` parameter of `organs/neural_language.py:6225 speak_sentence`, with `world/reasoning_agent.py:1334` as the existing call site that already passes allowed_pools -- but editing a live 6,900-line organ to route through a new flag is an organ change and gets its own design step and ruling, the same discipline as the H4 counter (docs/h4_updates_counter_design.md). Until that lands, this artifact measures the two rules, not the fly's decisions, and says so in its own quoting_guard.
candidate_routing_step3.numbering_correction: This is checklist step 3, not step 2. B.4 step 2 is 'Implement episodic replay at tiers 120 and 300 with the registered interference protocol', which is NOT implemented here and is blocked on D-MPE10-02 and D-MPE10-04. The routing work was requested as 'step 2'; it is recorded under the number the plan gives it, because a later reader who takes the wrong number will believe episodic replay exists.

test_result_measured.what_the_routing_tests_refuse_to_assert: no test claims one variant is better; that would be the answer to D-MPE10-03. They pin the flag surface, the exclusion semantics, the mask floor, that a selection does not mutate the trace (fingerprint before == after), and that the C5 test exists in the artifact.

what_the_ablation_measured.a_variant_won_only_with_the_other_disabl: 3 of 6 probes (variant_i's win survives only against `off`; on those probes it does not survive variant_ii)
what_the_ablation_measured.all_four_flags_agree: 1 of 6 probes (the repeated-token probe, where the state is unambiguous)
what_the_ablation_measured.battery: 6 fixed probes over a 12-word labelled stand-in alphabet, k=8, all four flags on each probe
what_the_ablation_measured.c5_handling: recorded as an ABLATION RESULT, not as a win for variant_ii. Nothing in this block confirms or swaps the registered primary; D-MPE10-03 stays open and this file does not answer it.
what_the_ablation_measured.the_structural_finding: the `both` condition returned the same winner as variant_ii on every probe, because a mask removes candidates before a drive can rank them. The two variants are therefore not additive: variant_ii SUBSUMES variant_i whenever both are enabled. That is the C5 shape discovered by measurement rather than by argument, and it is the substantive content D-MPE10-03 would be deciding on -- choosing (ii) as primary means (i) contributes nothing at runtime, and choosing (i) means giving up the exclusion semantics.

harness_hashes.note: Hashes are checkout-stable by construction. See seal_basis and the module docstring for the measurement behind it. reseal_history records every superseded value.

registrations_excluded.why: registrations are ledgers, not evidence. Two registrations that seal each other form a cycle no stamp sequence can satisfy, so cross-registration entries are dropped and the fact is recorded here rather than left as a DRIFT that never clears.

also_recorded: sha256_lf (equal to sha256_of_git_blob, proven per file)
seal_basis.chosen: (a) seal the git blob, not the worktree bytes
seal_basis.rejected: (b) a .gitattributes pinning eol -- it changes line-ending behaviour repository-wide, which is a policy decision, not a gate artifact
seal_basis.verification: tools/registration_seal.py --check recomputes both and asserts they agree
seal_basis.why: core.autocrlf=true with no .gitattributes means worktree bytes != blob bytes, so a worktree-byte seal cannot verify after commit+clone. Verified on the tracked 1.4 MB evidence file: worktree 1,473,837 CRLF bytes, blob 1,421,862 LF bytes, and `git hash-object` returns the index blob, so the conversion is applied.

self_excluded.why: a file listing its own hash is stale the moment the hash is written; --check can never be clean otherwise. Its content is still pinned transitively by the artifacts that cite it, and by git history.

stamp_ordering.note: git_dirty_sealed is the field to act on. A non-empty list means at least one file this seal hashes is not yet in the commit it names -- the seal is anchored to a commit that cannot reproduce it. Stamping a second registration right after the first is NOT that case, because registrations are excluded from every seal.
procedure: 2. run registration_seal.py <registration.json>   # git_head now contains those blobs
4. registration_seal.py <registration.json> --check   # must be clean at that HEAD
stamp_ordering.rule: COMMIT FIRST, THEN STAMP, THEN COMMIT THE STAMP. Never stamp while a file this seal hashes is uncommitted -- that is what git_dirty_sealed reports, not mere tree dirt.
stamp_ordering.why: git_head is the commit the seal claims to describe. If the sealed bytes are still uncommitted when the stamp is taken, git_head names a commit that does not contain them, and there is no checkout you can verify the seal against.

what_k_bounds.activation_trace: bounded by k -- the ring holds the last k tokens and nothing else
what_k_bounds.fast_weight_store: NOT bounded by k -- accumulates every adjacent pair until clear(); measured ||w||_F identical at k=2, k=8 and k=22 over a 64-token stream
what_k_bounds.reporting_obligation: Every MP-E10 artifact reports ||w||_F against tokens pushed as its own quantity, so a reader can never take 'capacity k' to mean the whole organ

k_sweep_calibration_tier40.checklist_step: G3 step 2, run in the registered order: tests first (23 passed in 0.16s), then the sweep, alone, with nothing else timed on the machine.
k_sweep_calibration_tier40.next_step_is_not_120_or_300: Tier 120 and tier 300 stay unrun. Not because of cost -- the sweep costs a quarter of a second -- but because a 'capacity-k arm' whose capacity bound does not apply to its own associative store is not the treatment the hypotheses name, and running the expensive tiers on it would produce numbers that cannot be attributed to anything.
k_sweep_calibration_tier40.quoting_guard_still_holds: No figure in this file may be quoted as evidence for or against H1 or H2 while those decisions are unresolved: H1's denominator and H2's scalar do not exist yet. This sweep does not resolve them either -- it says what the organ is, not how well Droso does.

three_findings_that_were_not_registered_.1: The fast-weight store is not bounded by k. The ring is bounded -- slots in use never exceeds k -- but ||w||_F is the same at k=2, k=8 and k=22 and grows with the NUMBER OF TOKENS PUSHED, not with k. The fast-weight state therefore has no capacity limit tied to k: it holds every adjacent pair the organ has ever seen until a restart. k bounds the activation trace, not the working memory as a whole.
three_findings_that_were_not_registered_.2: k=1, the first point of the registered grid, degenerates into self-links. No. At k=1 the state is exactly the sum of self-links and its diagonal mass is nonzero, while at k=2 and k=3 the diagonal mass is 0.0 and the state is the sum of adjacent pair-links. k=1 is the FIRST POINT OF THE REGISTERED GRID, so the grid's baseline is not a smaller version of the other points -- it is a different object.
three_findings_that_were_not_registered_.3: The store is a predecessor map, not a successor map. The store is a PREDECESSOR map: probing the later token returns the earlier one strongly, probing the earlier token does not return the later one. That is a coherent object, but it is the transpose of what a language-model working memory is normally asked to supply, and the registration does not say which one H1/H2 assume.
three_findings_that_were_not_registered_.how_found: By running the calibration the registration asked for. None of the 23 unit tests looked at any of these: they test decay bounds, restart clearing and the ring, and all three findings live in the part of the organ the tests do not probe.

k_sweep_calibration_tier40.what_it_does_not_establish: Nothing about H1 or H2. The alignment columns are k-invariant for k>=2 by construction -- read() consults only the fast-weight state, which does not depend on k -- so they are one number printed seven times, not a sweep result, and the artifact says so in the row itself. And the token vectors are a deterministic hash stand-in, not Droso's SAN projections, so every figure is a property of the trace.
k_sweep_calibration_tier40.what_it_establishes: The trace behaves as a bounded activation record: fully-held fraction rises 0% -> 33.96% -> 100% across k=1,4,8 and saturates at the longest taught utterance (7 tokens); the oldest slot's weight is exactly decay**(k-1); and the state separates an utterance from its reversal (order_separation falls from 1.018 at k=1 to 0.571 once the window holds the sentence) while the bag-of-words comparator it replaces scores 0.0 separation by construction.
k_sweep_calibration_tier40.what_the_sweep_actually_costs: 0.237s for the entire registered grid at tier 40. Calibration was never the expensive part of G3: the curriculum runs are. So the cost of running this sweep again after any organ decision is settled is negligible, and there is no reason to run 120/300 on an organ whose k semantics are still unresolved.
k_sweep_calibration_tier40.what_was_not_done: The sealed module was not edited. tools/mp_e10_working_memory.py is hashed in all four registrations' harness_hashes, and each finding changes what a registered quantity MEANS -- which is the class of change this repository has consistently routed to the PI rather than absorbing quietly (the sim_floor cells, the nearness bug, the H2 clause-2 basis).

objective_transcribed: Replace unigram context with a native, contextual sequence organ, and extend consolidation from the proven 40-item scale to the MP-E8 tiers. The episodic-write and replay-consolidation legs of the original three-timescale design are considered covered at 40 items by ELECTRIC C2 and C3 and are not re-proven at toy scale; this experiment carries them to scale and builds the missing seconds-scale timescale.

open_decisions_for_PI.D-MPE10-06_k_does_not_bound_the_fast_wei: RULED 2026-11-04 by PI -- see pi_decisions.rulings.D-MPE10-06_k_and_the_fast_weight_store. Not a defect: the plan describes two objects and the module implements two objects. k bounds the activation trace only; ||w||_F against tokens pushed is reported as its own quantity in every artifact. Organ not edited. Original text kept: The registered k is the capacity of a working memory, but the organ's associative state w accumulates every adjacent pair until clear() and its norm is identical at k=2, k=8 and k=22. Either k is meant to bound only the activation trace -- in which case H1/H2's 'capacity k' needs restating -- or the organ must decay/trim w with the window. open_decisions_for_PI.D-MPE10-07_k1_in_the_registered_grid_mea: RULED 2026-11-04 by PI -- see pi_decisions.rulings.D-MPE10-07_k_equals_1. k=1 excluded from the SCORED grid by AMD-MPE10-01, not deleted; diagonal mass still printed; the module's 'excluded by construction' claim corrected as a docstring-only edit. Original text kept: push() reads prev as a numpy view of ring[(head-1) % k] and then writes ring[head]; at k=1 those are the same slot, so the recorded 'pair' is outer(v_i, v_i). Measured: diagonal mass 3.679 at k=1 against -0.039 (i.e. zero) at every other k. The grid's baseline point is therefore a different object from the rest of the grid. Options: drop k=1 from the grid, or copy prev before the write. Registered as an instrument defect, not fixed unilaterally.
open_decisions_for_PI.D-MPE10-08_predecessor_or_successor_link: RULED 2026-11-04 by PI -- see pi_decisions.rulings.D-MPE10-08_read_direction. Organ not transposed; every artifact must name the direction it read; a successor map would be a registered organ change with its own design step. Original text kept: outer(post, pre) means probing the later token recovers the earlier one (cosine 0.982) and probing the earlier does not recover the later (0.056). A working memory feeding next-token behaviour needs the other transpose. The registration does not say which direction H1/H2 assume; settling it before any scored run is cheaper than discovering it in a curve.

D-MPE10-01_H1_denominator.ruled: H1's denominator is the FIVE pipeline stages stage_of() actually reports: gating, mouth, recall, recall_untraced, shape_arbiter. The plan's word 'four' is a v1.0 term that the v1.1 body never restates, so it is not a count of anything in this repository. 'Improve on at least two, none regressing' is unchanged.

D-MPE10-06_k_and_the_fast_weight_store.if_the_PI_later_wants_k_to_bound_the_sto: That is an organ change: re-seal and re-sweep. The sweep costs 0.237s at tier 40, so the cheap re-run is never the reason not to revisit it.
D-MPE10-06_k_and_the_fast_weight_store.reasoning: The plan describes two objects -- 'a decayed activation trace over the last k tokens' and 'a fast-weight state computed by spread' -- and the module implements exactly that. The sweep found ||w||_F identical at k=2, k=8 and k=22 over a 64-token stream, which is not a bug in the second object; it is the first object's bound failing to be read as the second one's. What was wrong was the description: 'capacity k' was being used as though it named the whole organ.
D-MPE10-06_k_and_the_fast_weight_store.ruled: k bounds the ACTIVATION TRACE only. The fast-weight store is unbounded until clear(), and that is the design, not a defect. Every MP-E10 artifact reports ||w||_F against tokens pushed as its own quantity.
D-MPE10-06_k_and_the_fast_weight_store.what_was_NOT_done: The organ was not edited. Bounding the store by k would be a different machine, and the ruling is about what to REPORT, not what to build.

D-MPE10-07_k_equals_1.behaviour_unchanged_proof: tests/test_mp_e10_working_memory.py: 23 passed in 0.17s after the edit (0.16s before).
D-MPE10-07_k_equals_1.docstring_corrected: tools/mp_e10_working_memory.py claimed self-links are 'excluded by construction'. At k=1 that is false, and a false claim in a sealed instrument is its own defect. The claim was corrected; the behaviour was not touched. A docstring fix is not a behaviour change, so the re-seal is bookkeeping and the only re-run is the 0.237s sweep -- nothing else.
D-MPE10-07_k_equals_1.reasoning: At k=1, (head-1) % k == head, so prev aliases the slot push() is about to overwrite and the 'pair' stored is outer(v, v) -- self-links. Measured: diagonal mass 3.679 at k=1 against -0.039 (zero) at every other k. A grid whose baseline point is a different object from the rest of the grid cannot be interpolated or compared, but deleting the point would destroy the evidence for the exclusion.
D-MPE10-07_k_equals_1.ruled: k=1 is registered as DEGENERATE and EXCLUDED from the grid used to score a run, by dated amendment experiments/MP-E10/results/ksweep_tier40_calibration.json. Excluded, not deleted: it stays in the registered grid and its diagonal mass keeps being printed, because the diagonal mass is the instrument that shows why it is degenerate.

D-MPE10-08_read_direction.discipline_precedent: MP-E8's nearness bug was measured, costed and ruled before it was fixed; the sim_floor cells were named rather than tolerated. This ruling keeps that shape.
D-MPE10-08_read_direction.reasoning: The mouth produces, which needs the successor direction; outer(post, pre) supplies the predecessor direction (measured 0.982 later-recovers-earlier against 0.056 earlier-recovers-later). Silently transposing the store would change what every previous measurement means, and it is the same class of move as quietly absorbing the sim_floor cells or the nearness bug: a fix that is really a redesign has to be seen to be a redesign.
D-MPE10-08_read_direction.ruled: The organ is not transposed. Every MP-E10 artifact must NAME WHICH DIRECTION it read -- the token probed and the token recovered -- and no figure may be reported as a bare 'alignment'. If a scored run requires the successor map, that is a registered organ change with its own design step.

what_these_rulings_do_and_do_not_authori.NOT_authorised: No scored MP-E10 run. D-MPE10-02 leaves H2 without a measure, D-MPE10-04 leaves the interference margin unconfirmed, and D-MPE10-05 leaves the question of running inside an open G2. Tiers 120 and 300 remain unrun by choice.
what_these_rulings_do_and_do_not_authori.authorised: Instrument preparation: the denominator is fixed, the organ's two objects are described correctly, the scored grid excludes k=1, and every artifact must declare its read direction.

D-MPE10-02.the_guardrails: Refusal rate and coverage are reported as the guardrails the plan already names ('without moving refusal or coverage backwards'). They are reported, not traded: a fluency gain that moves either backwards is not a fluency gain.
D-MPE10-02.the_ladder_is_not_reused: The mouth-stage ladder is NOT reused for H2. H1 already consumes it, and two hypotheses measured on one instrument is one hypothesis wearing two names.
D-MPE10-02.the_objection_registered_as_required: A longer answer is not necessarily a better answer, and this scalar rewards verbosity. It is therefore a DIRECTION-CHECK and not a quality measure, and it is recorded as such wherever it is used. The objection is registered in the same block as the ruling rather than in a footnote, because a metric whose weakness is buried reads like a metric that has none.
D-MPE10-02.the_scalar: H2's fluency scalar is the MEAN NUMBER OF CONTENT WORDS PER EMITTED ANSWER over the bench's live phase at that tier.
D-MPE10-02.what_this_unblocks_and_what_it_does_not: It makes H2 scoreable in principle, which it was not, and it removes the D-MPE10-02 half of the 'nothing in flight' blocker. It does not open step 2 or H3: those wait on D-MPE10-04 and D-MPE10-05. It also does not by itself produce a number -- the content-word count must be computed by the bench's existing word-level grader (R9) rather than by a new counter, and that is an implementation step with its own inertness question, the same shape as the H4 counter's.

D-MPE10-03.c5_consequence: A (ii) win is an ABLATION RESULT under C5 and does NOT demonstrate that the drive is worthless -- it is unmeasurable while the mask is on. Any scored run must state the (i)-alone figure alongside the (ii) figure rather than reporting the primary alone.
D-MPE10-03.option_rejected: (c) 'register the compound as primary' is REJECTED outright: the brief is right that the `both` condition is variant_ii with dead arithmetic attached -- it returned variant_ii's winner on every one of 6 probes.
D-MPE10-03.reason_recorded: (i) only re-weights among candidates that all remain legal, which is what spread already does, so it adds no new mechanism; and since the mask excludes candidates before the drive can rank them, (ii) determines the outcome whenever both are on. The choice is therefore really the design question the brief names -- MAY THE SEQUENCE ORGAN EVER MAKE A WORD ILLEGAL -- and the ruling is yes: hard admissibility is the organ's own existing discipline (allowed_pools, floored at 3 legal pools), and a re-weighting-only selection would be the same instrument the registration already criticises.
D-MPE10-03.ruling: Variant (ii) -- carve allowed_pools masking -- stays primary, exactly as the plan designates it. Variant (i) -- spread-scored selection -- is registered as the ABLATION that measures what re-weighting alone would have given.
D-MPE10-03.still_open: The house-side wiring is NOT authorised by this ruling: engine.decide / speak_sentence changes are an organ change with their own design step, named-missing in candidate_routing_step3.
D-MPE10-03.what_this_unblocks: B.4 step 4 (the four mouth-stage evaluations, the nine-axis suite, and the state-only / spread-only / state-plus-spread ablations) becomes scoreable, and G3's `go_if` can begin. Step 3 was already built and sealed.

conditions_three.1_row_count_travels_with_the_figure: every artifact carries the row count it divided by. A percentage-point claim without its denominator is the kind of number this program has had to un-buy twice (the 0.035 pp case, the 1.56x case).
conditions_three.2_report_an_interval_not_a_binary: interference is reported as a measured INTERVAL alongside the verdict, so a near-miss is visible rather than collapsed into pass/fail. A 1.9 pp result and a 0.1 pp result both clear 2.0 pp and are not the same finding.
conditions_three.3_re_measure_the_noise_input_at_the_tier: if the tier-300 clone set is ever run, the clone-noise input is re-measured AT THAT TIER and the margin re-derived BY AMENDMENT rather than carried over from tier-40 data. The derivation above is a statement about what tier-40 can show; carrying it to tier 300 silently would be borrowing a tolerance from a regime that was never measured.

D-MPE10-04.derivation_of_record: clone disagreement 11 rows of 3,672 = 0.2996 pp (registered in MP-E8 arms.N, re-verified on the current tree as [0, 1, 0] rows with the single movement inside the R13 time-dependent cell); tier-40 interference 0 regressions over 3 cycles x 53 items = 159 exposures; rule of three gives a 95% upper bound of 3/159 = 1.887 pp on a zero-event rate; 2.0 pp is that bound rounded up, and is 6.7x the measured clone noise. Row equivalent at tier 40: 2.7 rows of the 136-row probe matrix.
D-MPE10-04.options_rejected: (b) 5 pp is rejected as a round number inherited from a DIFFERENT experiment's noise floor (MP-E8's duel margin, chosen there against a different denominator); (c) refusing a margin and reporting H3 as an interval is rejected because it turns a go-criterion into a description, which is a plan amendment and not a ruling.
D-MPE10-04.ruling: Adopt (a): the interference margin is 2.0 percentage points, DERIVED, because it is the MORE demanding option and the derivation is shown.
D-MPE10-04.still_open: Nothing in this ruling scores H3. Step 2 is still unimplemented, and the replay mechanism it needs is ruled at -05 below but not yet built.
D-MPE10-04.what_this_unblocks: H3 becomes closeable in principle, and B.4 step 2's protocol becomes registrable (registered now, below, as interference_protocol_step2).

D-MPE10-05.option_C_noted: Replay through the plastic three-factor path (rate_core.py:580/:620, writing at :592/:629) is a DIFFERENT engram system and does not satisfy the plan's 'the same local rule that wrote the engrams' for sequence material. Not adopted.
D-MPE10-05.ruling: Option A is DISQUALIFIED by the project's own measurement. Adopt B: a dedicated replay entry with a registered replay gain that advances NEITHER transitions NOR sequences_learned, so the teaching counters stay honest.
D-MPE10-05.saturation_guard_pre_registered: REQUIRED, before any replay run. If ANY entry reaches the ceiling during a replay pass, that configuration is reported as CEILING-LIMITED and H3's interference number is VOID for it -- because SUCCESSOR_FLOOR 0.12 (sequence_organ.py:77) and SUCCESSOR_MARGIN 0.35 (:83) are ABSOLUTE gates that cannot survive a saturated store. The guard is a reporting rule, not a warning: a ceiling-limited run may not be scored.
D-MPE10-05.the_counters_asymmetry_recorded_as_the_r: 30 replay passes move sequences_learned +1,590 but transitions only +1,908 of the 6,360 an honest count would give -- because once nothing grows, `grew` is False and written stops accumulating. The counter that would reveal the drift is itself the one that saturates, so replay under A is not merely mis-counted: it is self-concealing.
D-MPE10-05.what_this_unblocks: B.4 step 2 now has an implementable form. It is an organ change on a live organ, so it carries the same inertness discipline as the H4 counter design step: the replay entry must not alter what a NON-replay run does, and `transitions` / `sequences_learned` must be provably untouched by replay.
D-MPE10-05.why_A_is_disqualified: A uniform translation that saturates at the 4.0 ceiling after 9 passes from the 3-cycle state (11 from a single cycle) and leaves distinct_weight_values = 1 at every pass, destroying exactly the ranking the readout needs. Measured in experiments/MP-E10/results/replay_rule_saturation_probe.json via tools/mp_e10_replay_rule_probe.py.

plan_source.note: embedded whole, because the thresholds below are only checkable against the wording they came from
plan_source.transcribed_verbatim: 6.3 MP-E10 - The Mouth and the Second Timescale Objective. Replace unigram context with a native, contextual sequence organ, and extend consolidation from the proven 40-item scale to the MP-E8 tiers. The episodic-write and replay-consolidation legs of the original three-timescale design are considered covered at 40 items by ELECTRIC C2 and C3 and are not re-proven at toy scale; this experiment carries them to scale and builds the missing seconds-scale timescale. Architecture. Seconds - working memory: plasticize the central-complex loop into a decayed activation trace over the last k tokens; a fast-weight state computed by spread, replacing unigram context; parameterize k and register its sweep. Selection - two native routing variants, both flag-gated: variant (i) scores candidates by spread of the decayed state plus target-organ injection (the target organ already injects into speak_sentence and is hereby actually used for selection); variant (ii) routes candidates through carve as an allowed_pools mask, the version closest to existing machinery. One variant is registered primary, the other the ablation. Consolidation at scale - replay through the same local rule that wrote the engrams (Hebbian co-activation with Oja-style normalization) at tiers 120 and 300, with interference measured against the MP-E8 curriculum. ===== PAGE 18 ===== DROSO Master Plan v1.1 | Live Brain Protocol 15 Hypotheses. H1: the four mouth-stage evaluations improve on at least two stages with none regressing. H2: fluency improves over the MP-E8 arm-A baseline at the same tier. H3: replay at tier 300 holds retention at the invariant with interference bounded by the pre- registered margin. H4: the invariants hold; regression on either is a hard reject under R6. C-conditions. C1: any untraceable word in generated output - abort (R9). C2: guarded rows answered - abort. C3: retention or restart survival regresses - abort. C4: working- memory state leaks across a restart - abort by definition (it is seconds-scale). C5: one routing variant wins only with the other disabled - record as ablation result, not a win. Gate G3. Go only if H1-H4 hold. On failure: the bigram-era organ stays as the fallback arm, and the routing ablation data decides the next attempt. Agent brief. Implement both routing variants behind flags; ablate state-only, spread-only, and state-plus-spread; keep the legacy path runnable for comparison; replay at the registered tiers with the interference protocol; emit per-stage results, the k-sweep grid, and decision.md.
